title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Thermal Expansion — 2021
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: A metal rod of length 1 m at 20 degrees C is heated to 100 degrees C. If the coefficient of linear expansivity of the metal is $1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, find the increase in length and the final length.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Given:** $L_0 = 1\ \text{m},\ T_1 = 20^\circ\text{C},\ T_2 = 100^\circ\text{C},\ \alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{K}^{-1}$

**Step 2 — Change in temperature:**
$$\Delta T = T_2 - T_1 = 100 - 20 = 80\ \text{K}$$

**Step 3 — Increase in length:**
$$\Delta L = \alpha L_0 \Delta T = (1.2 \times 10^{-5})(1)(80) = 96 \times 10^{-5} = 9.6 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{m}$$
$$\boxed{\Delta L = \mathbf{9.6 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{m}} = \mathbf{0.96\ \text{mm}}}$$

**Step 4 — Final length:**
$$L_2 = L_0 + \Delta L = 1 + 9.6 \times 10^{-4}$$
$$\boxed{L_2 = \mathbf{1.00096\ \text{m}}$$

**Note:** The expansion is very small, which is why gaps are left in railway tracks and bridges.
questions.knowledgeNote: Expansion equals alpha times original length times temperature rise; for a one-metre rod it is a fraction of a millimetre.
